title: Sickle cell (Glu6Val): DNA point mutation GAG -> GTG
vignette: A 14-year-old boy with chronic anemia is being evaluated after experiencing several episodes of chest, back, and extremity pain. Peripheral blood smear reveals sickle-shaped red blood cells. Genetic testing shows that the patient is homozygous for a point mutation in the beta-globin gene, resulting in a glutamic acid to valine substitution at position 6. Using the provided genetic code table, sequencing the affected DNA would most likely reveal which of the following changes?

clues.note: Sickled RBCs with vaso-occlusive pain crises indicate sickle cell disease.

clues.text: glutamic acid to valine substitution at position 6
clues.note: The sickle mutation replaces glutamate (Glu) with valine (Val) at position 6 of the beta-globin chain - a single-base missense mutation.

whatMatters: Sickle cell disease is a single-nucleotide MISSENSE mutation in beta-globin causing GLUTAMATE -> VALINE at codon 6. In DNA, glutamate is coded by GAA/GAG and valine by GTT/GTC/GTA/GTG; the single-base change that accomplishes it is GAG -> GTG (A->T at the middle position). Answer D.
strategy: Translate the amino-acid change into a DNA codon change using the table, remembering DNA uses T (not U). Glutamate = GAA or GAG; valine = GT_. A SINGLE base substitution linking them is GAG -> GTG (or GAA -> GTA). Pick the DNA option (GAG -> GTG). Reject the RNA option (GAA -> GUA - uracil isn't in DNA), multi-base changes, and codons that don't encode Glu->Val (e.g., a silent TTA->CTA).

eliminations.label: CAA -> GTT - not Glu->Val, multiple base changes
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: glutamine (CAA) to valine (GTT). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: the starting codon codes glutaMINE (not glutaMATE), and it requires multiple base changes - not the single Glu->Val substitution of sickle cell. ✅ Correct if: a different missense example.

eliminations.label: CAT -> CTT - histidine to leucine
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: histidine (CAT) to leucine (CTT). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: wrong amino acids entirely (not Glu->Val). ✅ Correct if: a His->Leu substitution.

eliminations.label: GAA -> GUA - RNA (uracil not in DNA)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: glutamate (GAA) to valine (GUA) - a valid single change but written in RNA. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: the question asks about DNA sequencing, and URACIL (U) does not occur in DNA (DNA uses thymine, T). ✅ Correct if: describing the mRNA-level change (GAA -> GUA).

eliminations.label: GTA -> GAA - valine to glutamate (reverse)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: valine (GTA) to glutamate (GAA) - the REVERSE direction. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: sickle cell is Glu->Val, not Val->Glu. ✅ Correct if: asking for the reverse substitution.

eliminations.label: TTA -> CTA - silent (both leucine)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: TTA and CTA both encode leucine. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it's a SILENT mutation (no amino-acid change) and involves leucine, not Glu->Val. ✅ Correct if: illustrating a silent mutation.

reasoning: Sickle cell = missense mutation, glutamate -> valine at beta-globin codon 6
Using the DNA code: glutamate = GAA/GAG; valine = GTT/GTC/GTA/GTG
The single-base substitution connecting them (with T, since it's DNA) is GAG -> GTG
mechanism: Sickle cell disease is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by a single-nucleotide POINT MUTATION in the coding region of the beta-globin gene, producing a MISSENSE change - glutamic acid (a hydrophilic, negatively charged residue) replaced by VALINE (hydrophobic) at position 6. This hydrophobic patch promotes polymerization of deoxygenated hemoglobin S, sickling red cells during hypoxic/stress states and causing painful vaso-occlusive episodes. Reading a genetic code TABLE (recalling that DNA uses THYMINE, not uracil): glutamate is encoded by GAA and GAG, and valine by GTT, GTC, GTA, and GTG. Comparing codons, the substitutions requiring only a SINGLE base change to convert Glu->Val are GAA->GTA and GAG->GTG; the classic sickle mutation is GAG -> GTG (an A->T change at the second position). The RNA-level equivalent is GAG->GUG (or GAA->GUA), but because the question asks about DNA, options containing uracil are incorrect. The other choices are wrong amino acids, multi-base changes, the reverse direction, or a silent mutation.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Convert Glu->Val to a single-base DNA codon change (use T, not U): GAG -> GTG.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on missense vs silent mutation, codon table, DNA (thymine) vs RNA (uracil), or Glu/Val codons? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: GAA->GUA is the RNA version (uracil not in DNA); other options are wrong amino acids, multi-base, reverse, or silent.

difficulty.label: 🖼️ Imaging / diagram
difficulty.text: On the codon table: find glutamate (GAA/GAG) and valine (GT_) and identify the single-base swap. Anchor: 'sickle = GAG -> GTG in DNA (GUG in mRNA).'

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: sickle cell = missense Glu6Val; DNA GAG -> GTG; hydrophobic valine drives HbS polymerization.

Silent = same amino acid; missense = different amino acid

memoryHook: Sickle swaps one letter: GAG (Glu) -> GTG (Val) in the DNA - a single A-to-T that makes hemoglobin sticky; the GUA/GUG versions belong to RNA, not DNA.
